headline: Broad-based growth lifts margins despite acquisition debt
summary_short: Morningstar's Q2 2026 revenue rose 9.6% y/y to $663.2M, with operating income up 28.4% y/y to $160.6M and diluted EPS up 35.4% y/y to $2.83, as license-, asset-, and transaction-based revenue all grew and CRSP lifted Morningstar Indexes 85.3%.
summary_long: Revenue grew 9.6% y/y to $663.2M, led by license-based growth in Direct Platform and PitchBook, 17.5% asset-based growth from Retirement and Wealth, and 18.0% transaction-based growth from Morningstar Credit. CRSP, acquired in February for $363.0M, drove Indexes revenue up 85.3%. Operating margin expanded 3.5pp to 24.2% as revenue growth outpaced expenses. Diluted EPS rose 35.4% y/y to $2.83, helped by a 10.4% drop in diluted shares under an ongoing $1.0B buyback ($700M repurchased to date). Long-term debt roughly doubled y/y to $1,695.1M after Morningstar drew a new credit facility partly to fund CRSP; cash fell slightly to $489.5M. No forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: Revenue grew across all three revenue types (license, asset, transaction-based), with Morningstar Credit and CRSP-driven Indexes the fastest growers; operating margin expanded 3.5pp as revenue growth outpaced expense growth.

License-based revenue grew on Direct Platform and PitchBook demand; asset-based grew on Morningstar Retirement and Wealth product sales; transaction-based grew on Morningstar Credit issuance activity.
Tracks the 9.6% revenue increase against a much smaller 3.8% rise in cost of revenue, widening gross margin.

Increase reflects $58.1 million higher revenue and $6.0 million higher other operating income, partly offset by $28.6 million higher operating expense, mainly G&A compensation and CRSP-related intangible amortization.
Tracks the operating-income increase; EBIT differs slightly from operating income due to non-operating income/expense items.
Tracks the operating-income increase plus higher intangible amortization added back, primarily from CRSP-related intangibles.

Operating income growth was partly offset by a higher effective tax rate (26.2% vs 22.8% y/y) from deferred taxes on unremitted foreign earnings and a stock-vesting tax impact.
EPS grew faster than net income because diluted shares fell 10.4% y/y under the ongoing $1.0 billion buyback program.
Tracks the diluted EPS trend: net income growth plus a lower share count from buybacks.
Cash declined slightly as $359.6 million paid for the CRSP acquisition and cumulative buybacks/dividends were only partly offset by higher operating cash flow and new credit-facility borrowings.
Debt roughly doubled after Morningstar entered a new $1.5 billion credit agreement in October 2025, drawing funds to help finance the CRSP acquisition.
Decline is consistent with cumulative $700 million of share buybacks since October 2025 plus dividends paid, which together exceeded retained net income over the trailing year.
Weighted diluted shares fell as Morningstar repurchased shares totaling $700 million cumulative under its $1.0 billion, three-year buyback program launched in October 2025.
